title: Feature/2170
summary: Before this change, if you were writing a note and clicked the number of a verse that already had notes (or the notes button in the phone header), the Discover pane switched to the notes list and your typed text vanished without a warning. Now Seed Bible asks **Discard your note?** first, with **Keep editing** and **Discard note** buttons. The same question now also appears when you choose **Cancel**, the back arrow, or the pane's close button, or start or edit a different note, while the note has unsaved text. A note with nothing typed (or no changes) still closes straight away without asking.

links.label: Issue 2170: Note editor loses unsaved text when the reader switches Discover to its notes

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a laptop or desktop, with the window wide (not phone-sized). Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old version, do a hard refresh: **Ctrl+Shift+R** (Windows) or **Cmd+Shift+R** (Mac).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email address. You'll get a code by email, so use an inbox you can check. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start if anything looks odd.

setup.title: Turn off "Show discovered content"
setup.body: Open **Settings**, find the **Discovered Content** heading, and make sure **Show discovered content** is **unchecked**. This makes notes open in the Discover side pane, which is where the lost-text problem happened. (One test near the end turns it back on.)

setup.title: Make one saved note to click on
setup.body: Open **John 3**. Click verse 16 to select it, choose **Note** from the menu that appears, type `First note`, and choose **Save**. Verse 16's number now shows that it has a note. You'll click that verse number in several tests.

sections.title: The warning when leaving an unsaved note
sections.intro: The main fix: clicking an annotated verse number while writing a note.

tests.title: Clicking a verse number with notes asks before throwing away a new note
tests.why: This is the exact repro from issue 2170.
tests.before: You're on John 3 with the note on verse 16 from setup.
steps: Click verse **18** to select it and choose **Note**.
Type `Draft one` in the note editor. Don't save.
Click the small number of verse **16** (the one with a note).
expected: A box titled **Discard your note?** appears, saying "You have an unsaved note. Discard it, or keep editing?", with **Keep editing** and **Discard note** buttons.
Behind it, the note editor is still showing with `Draft one` in it.

tests.title: Keep editing leaves your text in place
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, with the **Discard your note?** box open.
steps: Choose **Keep editing**.
expected: The box closes.
The note editor is still open with `Draft one` in it, and you can keep typing.
Discover did **not** switch to the notes list.

tests.title: Discard note drops the text and shows the verse's notes
tests.before: Continue from the previous test, with `Draft one` still in the editor.
steps: Click the number of verse **16** again.
In the **Discard your note?** box, choose **Discard note**.
expected: The box closes and Discover shows the notes list, scrolled to verse 16 with `First note` visible.
No note with `Draft one` was saved (it's not in the list).

tests.title: An empty note closes without asking
tests.why: Nothing typed means nothing to lose, so there should be no prompt.
steps: Click verse **18** to select it and choose **Note**. Don't type anything.
Click the number of verse **16**.
expected: No **Discard your note?** box appears.
Discover switches straight to the notes list at verse 16.

tests.title: Saving still works and doesn't ask
steps: Click verse **18** to select it and choose **Note**.
Type `Saved second note` and choose **Save**.
expected: No **Discard your note?** box appears.
The note is saved and shows in the notes list for verse 18.

sections.title: Other ways of leaving the editor
sections.intro: The PR also asks before leaving through these buttons. Each test starts by opening a new note on verse 20 and typing some text.

tests.title: Cancel asks when there's unsaved text
steps: Select verse **20**, choose **Note**, and type `Cancel test`.
Choose **Cancel** under the editor.
In the box, choose **Keep editing**.
Choose **Cancel** again, and this time choose **Discard note**.
expected: The first **Cancel** shows the **Discard your note?** box, and **Keep editing** leaves `Cancel test` in the editor.
After **Discard note**, the editor closes and Discover goes back to what it showed before you started the note. No `Cancel test` note is saved.

tests.title: The back arrow asks when there's unsaved text
steps: Select verse **20**, choose **Note**, and type `Back test`.
Click the back arrow (**Back**) at the top left of the editor, next to the **Annotate** title.
expected: The **Discard your note?** box appears. **Keep editing** keeps the text; **Discard note** closes the editor without saving.

tests.title: Closing the Discover pane asks when there's unsaved text
steps: Select verse **20**, choose **Note**, and type `Close test`.
Click the close button (X) of the Discover pane.
expected: The **Discard your note?** box appears instead of the pane closing.
**Keep editing** leaves the pane open with `Close test`; **Discard note** closes the pane and saves nothing.

tests.title: Editing an existing note: no changes closes freely, changes ask
steps: In the Discover notes list, open the options menu (**Annotation options**, the ⋮ button) on `First note` and choose **Edit**.
Without changing anything, choose **Cancel**.
Choose **Edit** on `First note` again, add the word ` changed` to the end, and choose **Cancel**.
Choose **Discard note**.
expected: The first **Cancel** (no changes) closes the editor with no box.
The second **Cancel** (after typing) shows **Discard your note?**.
After **Discard note**, the note in the list still reads `First note` without ` changed`.

tests.title: Choosing Note again while a note is unsaved asks first
steps: Select verse **20**, choose **Note**, and type `Other note test`.
Click verse **22** to select it, and choose **Note** from the menu.
expected: The **Discard your note?** box appears before a new note starts.
**Keep editing** keeps `Other note test` on screen; **Discard note** starts a fresh, empty note.
tests.why: Starting a new note used to replace the one being written without asking.

sections.title: Phone width
sections.intro: Issue 2170 names the notes button in the phone-size reader header as the second way text was lost.

setup.title: Make the window phone-sized
setup.body: Either open the preview on a phone (signed in to the same account), or narrow your browser window until the reader switches to its phone layout. **Show discovered content** must still be off.

tests.title: The header notes button asks before throwing away a note
tests.before: You're on John 3, which has saved notes from earlier tests.
steps: Select a verse without a note (for example verse **22**), choose **Note**, and type `Phone draft`.
Tap the notes button in the reader header (its label reads like **2 notes for this chapter**).
expected: The **Discard your note?** box appears, and the editor still has `Phone draft`.
**Keep editing** keeps the text. Tapping the button again and choosing **Discard note** shows the notes list at the first verse with a note.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: With "Show discovered content" on, clicking a verse number doesn't lose a note silently
tests.why: The PR also routes this setting's path through the new check, so clicking a verse number while editing now may close the editor here too. Neither the issue nor the PR says what should happen in this mode; the one firm rule is that typed text is never lost without asking.
tests.before: Back on a wide window. In **Settings**, check **Show discovered content**.
steps: On John 3, select verse **20**, choose **Note**, and type `Inline test`.
Click the number of verse **16**.
expected: Either the editor stays open with `Inline test`, or the **Discard your note?** box appears. The text is never gone without a prompt.
The notes for verse 16 are shown (beside the text or in the pane).

tests.title: Clicking a verse number when no note is being written works as before
steps: Make sure no note editor is open.
Click the number of verse **16**.
expected: No **Discard your note?** box appears, and the notes for verse 16 show right away, as before.

notCovered: Replying to a note from **Your content** (the path from PR 2169) isn't tested here; it isn't changed by this PR's code.
The new code paths are also covered by automated tests in the PR (unit tests for the note editor and the notes manager).
